emergency.title: If you or someone near you has symptoms
emergency.short: Contact your national health hotline or local health authorities immediately.
emergency.symptoms: Sudden fever, severe tiredness, muscle pain, headache or sore throat, sometimes followed by vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding.
emergency.action: Contact your national health hotline or local health authorities immediately. Say if the person has been near someone ill with Ebola. Early care improves the chance of survival.
emergency.care: Avoid touching the sick person's blood or other body fluids. Do not touch the body of someone who may have died of Ebola: the health authorities can arrange a safe and dignified burial.

about.heading: About Ebola.help
about.what: Ebola.help is an independent public information service. It gathers official updates, news coverage, helplines and prevention advice about Ebola disease in Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish.
about.independence: Ebola.help is not affiliated with, endorsed by or speaking for the World Health Organization (WHO), any other United Nations agency, Africa CDC or any government. It has no official status. Always follow the instructions of your national health authorities.
about.who: Ebola.help is run by {name}, a journalist and translator based in Cairo, who is responsible for everything published on the site. Ebola.help is not a health authority: every health page is based only on official public health sources, and links to them. The site does not speak for any government or international organisation.
about.sources: Our health pages, figures and situation updates use only official sources: WHO (including its Regional Office for Africa), the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), Africa CDC and the Ministry of Public Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Each helpline is checked against an official source before it is published. For news articles we show only the headline, the source and the date, with a link to the full article on the publisher's website.
about.verification: Every phone number, address and health facility on this site is checked against an official source. Each one shows that source and the date it was last verified. If we cannot verify a detail, we do not publish it.
about.translation: News is shown in its original language, labelled with that language. If a headline is ever shown in machine translation, it is clearly marked as such, together with the original language.
about.medical: This site gives general information only. It does not replace doctors, nurses or other health workers. If you feel ill, contact a health worker or your national health hotline.
about.advertising: To cover its costs, the home page, the news pages and the map show ads from Google AdSense. Pages with health advice and helplines never show ads. Ads are chosen automatically by Google: they are not recommendations, and advertisers have no influence on the content of this site. No ads are loaded on data-saving or very slow connections.
about.support: Ebola.help is free for everyone and receives no official funding. If you find it useful, you can help cover its costs on {patreon}. Supporters have no influence on what we publish.
about.privacy: We do not collect personal information ourselves. The site stores one small cookie to remember your language. Google and other advertising companies use cookies to show ads, which may be based on your previous visits to this and other websites ({googleUse}). You can turn off personalised ads in {adsSettings} or at {aboutAds}. Visitors in Europe, the United Kingdom and Switzerland are asked for their consent first.

about.contact: If you find a wrong phone number or any other error, please write to {email}.
